lesson.text: Quick memory: what do you do if your tower falls down? (Try again!) Today: true stories of people who kept going.
Louis Braille could not see. When he was 15 he made letters of six dots you can feel. Blind people read braille all over the world.
Wangari Maathai started with a few trees. With many friends, more than 50 million trees have been planted.
The Wright brothers' gliders kept coming down. They tested, fixed and tried again, and in 1903 they flew.
These people kept going, worked as a team and tried again. You can too.
Try it in the Story Theatre: help the buddies act their stories.
